## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.

- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. ## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json          # 6 gh-1028 engine cases + full smAgent suite

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. ## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. ## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. ## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. ## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 1032
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1032
- **Title**: gh-1028 Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1028` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +550
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T08:47:33Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:50:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json          # 6 gh-1028 engine cases + full smAgent suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json              # 3873 passed, 0 failed
```

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1032
- **Title**: gh-1028 Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1028` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +550
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T08:47:33Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:50:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json          # 6 gh-1028 engine cases + full smAgent suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json              # 3873 passed, 0 failed

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.
