# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

1. **Guard breadth — non-rework dispatches also suppressed.** The guard lives in triggerWorkflow and fires for any rule whose workflowRef resolves to the item's branch. That includes review legs, dev legs, test-automation legs. Is suppression there correct? Two legs one branch race pushes — yes, single-writer is the right premise for all leg types on the same branch. And the label/arm survives so it re-fires. I think it's defensible. But one scenario: rework-on-label fires while a review leg is legitimately in flight on the branch (review leg addressing review comments — pushes). Supressing rework is right.

  Another scenario: **two different tickets sharing a branch**? Not in this factory (branch per ticket).

2. **Deadlock/starvation scenario**: leg A in flight on branch; the tick suppresses arm; leg A completes without consuming the PR arm label (e.g. the leg was a DEV leg, not a rework leg — the rework arm waits). Leg A finishes → next tick dispatches. OK.

  Worse: an `in_progress` run wedged forever (hung runner) suppresses indefinitely. Comment says in_progress never ages out deliberately. A hung GitHub run eventually gets cancelled by timeout usually. The arm stays armed; owner cancel the run. Acceptable design trade-off, documented.

3. **`updated_at`-based staleness for queued runs**: a queued run that is actively moving (updated_at fresh) but stuck in queue behind a concurrency group for >6h ages out only if updated_at is stale — fine, mirrors smAgent.

4. **matchesBranch type-tolerance with number head_branch**: `String(run.head_branch) === String(branch)` — if branch is '100' and run head_branch is 100 → match. Edge: branch '01000' vs 100 — String(100)='100' ≠ '01000'. Fine.

5. **Pure module quality**: clean, GralJS-safe (var, no arrow functions), JSON-safe. Follows pack-require rule (hoisted). Tests comprehensive: 16 pure cases + 6 engine cases covering AC1/AC2.

Could merge into one pass sharing runs, since the branch check can be applied to the same fetched runs. Actually, hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun matches on title token; its fetched runs include head_branch presumably, so the branch probe could reuse... but a fetch for status X is done twice. Minor perf; the tick already does these probes. I'll flag as SUGESTION.

8. **Issue: guard also applies to `workflowRef` that literally equals the branch without substitution** — e.g., a rule hardcoding workflowRef: 'ai/gh-100'. Same semantics. Fine.

## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

While that runs, let me continue the deep review. Points to evaluate:

1. **Guard breadth — non-rework dispatches also suppressed.** The guard lives in triggerWorkflow and fires for any rule whose workflowRef resolves to the item's branch. That includes review legs, dev legs, test-automation legs. Is suppression there correct? Two legs one branch race pushes — yes, single-writer is the right premise for all leg types on the same branch. And the label/arm survives so it re-fires. I think it's defensible. But one scenario: rework-on-label fires while a review leg is legitimately in flight on the branch (review leg addressing review comments — pushes). Supressing rework is right.

  Another scenario: **two different tickets sharing a branch**? Not in this factory (branch per ticket).

2. **Deadlock/starvation scenario**: leg A in flight on branch; the tick suppresses arm; leg A completes without consuming the PR arm label (e.g. the leg was a DEV leg, not a rework leg — the rework arm waits). Leg A finishes → next tick dispatches. OK.

  Worse: an `in_progress` run wedged forever (hung runner) suppresses indefinitely. Comment says in_progress never ages out deliberately. A hung GitHub run eventually gets cancelled by timeout usually. The arm stays armed; owner cancel the run. Acceptable design trade-off, documented.

3. **`updated_at`-based staleness for queued runs**: a queued run that is actively moving (updated_at fresh) but stuck in queue behind a concurrency group for >6h ages out only if updated_at is stale — fine, mirrors smAgent.

4. **matchesBranch type-tolerance with number head_branch**: `String(run.head_branch) === String(branch)` — if branch is '100' and run head_branch is 100 → match. Edge: branch '01000' vs 100 — String(100)='100' ≠ '01000'. Fine.

5. **Pure module quality**: clean, GralJS-safe (var, no arrow functions), JSON-safe. Follows pack-require rule (hoisted). Tests comprehensive: 16 pure cases + 6 engine cases covering AC1/AC2.

6. **Test style nit**: `assert.notOk(x === false, ...)` double negative in two tests (lines ~124-130 of test_branchLegGuard.js). Should be `assert.ok(x)`. SUGESTION.

7. **Duplicated fan-out**: hasActiveLegRunOnBranch duplicates hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun's per-status listWorkflowRuns loop — up to 8 API calls per dispatch now. Could merge into one pass sharing runs, since the branch check can be applied to the same fetched runs. However they key differently (name token vs branch), and merging would couple two guards; parity approach is defensible. SUGESTION at most. Actually, hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun matches on title token; its fetched runs include head_branch presumably, so the branch probe could reuse... but a fetch for status X is done twice. Minor perf; the tick already does these probes. I'll flag as SUGESTION.

8. **Issue: guard also applies to `workflowRef` that literally equals the branch without substitution** — e.g., a rule hardcoding workflowRef: 'ai/gh-100'. Same semantics. Fine.

9. **Order of guards**: gh-1028 guard runs AFTER gh-715 cross-anchor. If the cross-anchor suppressed and consumed labels... gh-715 consume happens on skipInfo.crossAnchorActive — before gh-1028. That's intended behavior parity. But consider the reverse: gh-1028 suppresses (return false, no skipInfo) → label NOT consumed (correct per design). Good.

10. **Concurrency between probe and dispatch**: two ticks simultaneously probing both see no run and both dispatch — inherent race, same as gh-806 latch. Not new.

11. **`Date.now()`** — fine in GralJS.

12. **Check: `parseWorkflowRuns` handles mock shapes** — already used. Fine.

13. **Check run_all.json ordering**: test_branchLegGuard.js added to run_all list. And run_branchLegGuard.json created. Fine.

14. Line numbers for inline comments: I need lines in the diff. Let me get exact line numbers in the new files for my findings:

Finding candidates:
- SUGESTION: `assert.notOk(... === false ...)` double-negative assertions in test_branchLegGuard.js (two sites: "a queued run with NO timestamps is never stale" test ~line 124).
- SUGESTION: duplicated 4-status listWorkflowRuns fan-out — could share one fetch pass with hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun (js/smAgent.js ~line 374, function hasActiveLegRunOnBranch).
- SUGESTION or IMPORTANT?: The guard suppression applies to ALL rules landing on a branch, not just rework arms — including first-time dev dispatches for a story whose branch already has... actually no other story uses the branch. Hmm.

Let me think about whether there's any real BLOCKING/IMPORTANT issue.

**Potential correctness gap — the probe only lists runs for `workflowFile`**: `scm.listWorkflowRuns(status, workflowFile, 50)` filters by workflow file, then isLegRun double-checks the path suffix. Fine.

**Page size 50**: if >50 active runs of ai-teammate.yml across the repo, the target branch's run may beyond page 1 and the probe misses it → duplicate leg. Same limitation as the existing gh-806 latch (parity, page 50). Existing pattern; not a regression. Could mention as SUGESTION (parity-bound documented).

**What about `workflowRuns` queued status check ordering**: 'waiting'/'pending' are GitHub check-run statuses, not workflow run statuses. GitHub workflow run statuses: queued, in_progress, completed, requested, waiting, pending (pending exists for runs). Fine — superset matching is fail-closed.

**One real design question — dev leg + rework arm on the same branch at the SAME tick**: the AC1 test shows two arms in one tick → exactly one leg. What about a review leg in flight and the rework-on-label arm fires? Supressed, label survives, re-fires next tick. Good.

**What about the reverse hazard**: an in-flight TEST-AUTOMATION leg on the branch suppressing a rework dispatch — but test automation legs don't push usually... suppression is conservative, arm re-fires. Fine.

**Doc nit in the pure module header**: "the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists" — the new probe re-lists rather than reusing the tick's existing probe. Ties to the perf suggestion.

Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json          # 6 gh-1028 engine cases + full smAgent suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json              # 3873 passed, 0 failed
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Two legs one branch race pushes — yes, single-writer is the right premise for all leg types on the same branch. And the label/arm survives so it re-fires. I think it's defensible. But one scenario: rework-on-label fires while a review leg is legitimately in flight on the branch (review leg addressing review comments — pushes). Supressing rework is right.

  Another scenario: **two different tickets sharing a branch**? Not in this factory (branch per ticket).

2. **Deadlock/starvation scenario**: leg A in flight on branch; the tick suppresses arm; leg A completes without consuming the PR arm label (e.g. the leg was a DEV leg, not a rework leg — the rework arm waits). Leg A finishes → next tick dispatches. OK.

  Worse: an `in_progress` run wedged forever (hung runner) suppresses indefinitely. Comment says in_progress never ages out deliberately. A hung GitHub run eventually gets cancelled by timeout usually. The arm stays armed; owner cancel the run. Acceptable design trade-off, documented.

3. **`updated_at`-based staleness for queued runs**: a queued run that is actively moving (updated_at fresh) but stuck in queue behind a concurrency group for >6h ages out only if updated_at is stale — fine, mirrors smAgent.

4. **matchesBranch type-tolerance with number head_branch**: `String(run.head_branch) === String(branch)` — if branch is '100' and run head_branch is 100 → match. Edge: branch '01000' vs 100 — String(100)='100' ≠ '01000'. Fine.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

```bash

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. ## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_branchLegGuard.json   # 14 pure-module cases
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json          # 6 gh-1028 engine cases + full smAgent suite

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

1. **Guard breadth — non-rework dispatches also suppressed.** The guard lives in triggerWorkflow and fires for any rule whose workflowRef resolves to the item's branch. That includes review legs, dev legs, test-automation legs. Is suppression there correct? Two legs one branch race pushes — yes, single-writer is the right premise for all leg types on the same branch. And the label/arm survives so it re-fires. I think it's defensible. But one scenario: rework-on-label fires while a review leg is legitimately in flight on the branch (review leg addressing review comments — pushes). Supressing rework is right.

  Another scenario: **two different tickets sharing a branch**? Not in this factory (branch per ticket).

2. **Deadlock/starvation scenario**: leg A in flight on branch; the tick suppresses arm; leg A completes without consuming the PR arm label (e.g. the leg was a DEV leg, not a rework leg — the rework arm waits). Leg A finishes → next tick dispatches. OK.

  Worse: an `in_progress` run wedged forever (hung runner) suppresses indefinitely. Comment says in_progress never ages out deliberately. A hung GitHub run eventually gets cancelled by timeout usually. The arm stays armed; owner cancel the run. Acceptable design trade-off, documented.

3. **`updated_at`-based staleness for queued runs**: a queued run that is actively moving (updated_at fresh) but stuck in queue behind a concurrency group for >6h ages out only if updated_at is stale — fine, mirrors smAgent.

4. **matchesBranch type-tolerance with number head_branch**: `String(run.head_branch) === String(branch)` — if branch is '100' and run head_branch is 100 → match. Edge: branch '01000' vs 100 — String(100)='100' ≠ '01000'. Fine.

## PR Description

Closes #1028
### What changed
Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

### Key decisions
- Probe keys on the **branch**, not the head: the live duplicate (PR #1017, 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z) survived because the first leg's push moved the head, giving the gh-806 `(pr, head)` latch a new key, and the PR-armed factory run title (`workflow_dispatch # rework`) carries no anchor token for the gh-715/gh-944 title guards.
- Guard lives in `triggerWorkflow` (the common choke point of both dispatch paths), applied whenever the dispatch lands on the item's branch (`workflowRef={branch}`).
- Suppression does **not** consume the `agent:rework` label (unlike the gh-715 cross-anchor consume): a silently dead leg leaves the arm armed and the next quiet tick re-fires it — dead-letter recovery intact.
- Stale non-running runs (queued/waiting/pending >6h) age out; `in_progress` never ages out; probe errors fail open (one stacked leg beats a wedged rework loop).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Added a branch-keyed in-flight leg guard (gh-1028): `js/common/branchLegGuard.js` (pure probe — an ACTIVE `ai-teammate.yml` run whose `head_branch` IS the dispatch branch, regardless of `head_sha`, owns the branch) wired into `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, so BOTH rework dispatch arms (issue-anchored `rework-on-red-ci` and PR-anchored `rework-on-label`) suppress a second leg while one is in flight on the PR branch.

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# gh-1028: Duplicate concurrent rework legs on one PR (issue-arm + PR-arm both dispatch; head-move defeats the (pr,head) latch)

## Description

Live evidence 2026-10-18 08:04–08:09Z: PR #1017 (ticket gh-1000, branch ai/gh-1000) got TWO concurrent rework legs for the same rework cycle:
- run 39110030366 (08:04:12Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch # rework") — PR-anchored dispatch from the rework-on-label path (PR carried agent:rework)
- run 39110364398 (08:09:31Z, displayTitle "workflow_dispatch #1000 rework") — issue-anchored dispatch from rework-on-red-ci (issue gh-1000 carried agent:rework)

Both legs checkout/rewrite the same branch ai/gh-1000 concurrently → token waste ×2 and a push race (second pusher lands on a moved checkout).

## Why the dedupe missed it
The gh-806 AC1 in-flight latch is keyed (pr, head). Between the two dispatches the head moved (c2e0d28f → 94988905 — silent-update / first leg's push), so the second dispatch saw a different latch key and fired. Additionally the two dispatch paths (issue-arm rule vs PR-arm rule) appear to consult the latch independently of each other's in-flight runs — neither probed "is ANY teammate run already in flight for this PR".

## Fix direction
- The rework dispatch gate should probe live AI Teammate runs by branch/PR (the tick already lists in-flight teammate runs in its log — that probe exists) regardless of head, for BOTH dispatch paths (issue-anchored and PR-anchored).
- Or: single-carrier arm — conflict/verdict arms land on ONE carrier (issue xor PR) so two rules can never both dispatch the same PR.

## Acceptance
- [ ] An issue-armed and PR-armed rework for the SAME PR dispatches exactly one leg.
- [ ] A head move between dispatches does not bypass the in-flight probe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).
