## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: The gh-1028 branch-keyed in-flight leg guard correctly closes the duplicate-concurrent-rework hole the (pr, head) latch and the title guards both missed (live PR #1017): both rework dispatch arms flow through `smAgent.triggerWorkflow`, the probe keys on `head_branch` regardless of `head_sha` (AC2), and suppression deliberately does not consume the `agent:rework` label so a silently dead leg re-fires on the next quiet tick. AC1/AC2 are covered by 16 pure-module cases plus 6 engine cases, and the full suite is green (3895 passed, 0 failed).

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` is the third identical 4-status `listWorkflowRuns` fan-out in `smAgent.js` — up to 12 API calls per branch dispatch; extract a shared per-status fetch helper.
- 💡 Double-negative assertion (`assert.notOk(x === false)`) in `test_branchLegGuard.js`.
- 💡 Page-size 50 parity bound: >50 active leg runs repo-wide can push the owning run off page 1 (same bound as the gh-806 latch — worth a shared constant/comment).

**Next Steps**:
1. Merge as-is, or extract the shared active-run fan-out helper in a follow-up.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: third identical 4-status `listWorkflowRuns` fan-out — extract a shared helper**

`hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` re-implements the exact same per-status fan-out that already exists twice in this file:

- `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` (line ~334) — the gh-806 title-token latch
- `collectActiveWorkflowRuns` (line ~441) — the budget/summary collector

All three loop `['queued','in_progress','waiting','pending']`, call `scm.listWorkflowRuns(status, workflowFile, 50)`, wrap in the same try/`console.warn`/`continue`, and run through `parseWorkflowRuns`. This is now the third copy of the same transport loop, and it has a real cost: a dispatch that lands on a branch pays up to **12 `listWorkflowRuns` API round-trips per tick** (3 guards × 4 statuses) in the common nothing-in-flight case — plus the latency on every suppression decision.

Suggest extracting one transport primitive, e.g.:

```javascript
// Returns { runsByStatus: { queued: [...], ... }, errors: [...] } — one fan-out.
function listActiveRunsByStatus(scm, workflowFile) { ... }
```

and letting all three consumers filter the parsed runs they need (title-token match, branch match, summary formatting). That keeps each guard's pure predicate untouched while deduplicating the only part that actually repeats. Not merge-blocking — the parity comment shows the duplication was a deliberate choice — but the repo's own conventions (pure module + thin transport half) point at this extraction.

💡 **SUGGESTION: double-negative assertion — use `assert.ok`**

```javascript
assert.notOk(guard.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, BRANCH, { nowMs: NOW_MS }) === false,
    'no timestamp -> not stale -> still owns the branch');
```

`assert.notOk(x === false)` asserts the same thing as `assert.ok(x)` but makes the reader do two negation flips to see it — and if the helper ever returned `undefined`/non-boolean the two forms would diverge silently. Prefer the direct positive form:

```javascript
assert.ok(guard.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, BRANCH, { nowMs: NOW_MS }),
    'no timestamp -> not stale -> still owns the branch');
```

💡 **SUGGESTION: page-size 50 is a silent correctness bound — make it a named constant shared with the gh-806 latch**

```javascript
runs = parseWorkflowRuns(scm.listWorkflowRuns(statuses[i], workflowFile, 50));
```

The probe only sees the first 50 runs per status. If the repo ever has more than 50 active `ai-teammate.yml` runs, the leg that owns this branch can fall off page 1 and the guard silently misses it — the exact duplicate-leg pathology this PR exists to prevent returns, with no warning. This is **parity** with `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` (same hard-coded 50), so it's not a regression — but the bound is now load-bearing in two independent guards and deserves a single named constant (e.g. `ACTIVE_RUN_PROBE_PAGE = 50`) with a comment, so a future bump fixes both call sites at once. Optionally log when a status page comes back full (`runs.length === 50`), which is the only cheap in-band signal that the probe may be blind.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

  Another scenario: **two different tickets sharing a branch**? Not in this factory (branch per ticket).

2. **Deadlock/starvation scenario**: leg A in flight on branch; the tick suppresses arm; leg A completes without consuming the PR arm label (e.g. the leg was a DEV leg, not a rework leg — the rework arm waits). Leg A finishes → next tick dispatches. OK.

  Worse: an `in_progress` run wedged forever (hung runner) suppresses indefinitely. Comment says in_progress never ages out deliberately. A hung GitHub run eventually gets cancelled by timeout usually. The arm stays armed; owner cancel the run. Acceptable design trade-off, documented.

3. **`updated_at`-based staleness for queued runs**: a queued run that is actively moving (updated_at fresh) but stuck in queue behind a concurrency group for >6h ages out only if updated_at is stale — fine, mirrors smAgent.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: third identical 4-status `listWorkflowRuns` fan-out — extract a shared helper**

`hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` re-implements the exact same per-status fan-out that already exists twice in this file:

- `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` (line ~334) — the gh-806 title-token latch
- `collectActiveWorkflowRuns` (line ~441) — the budget/summary collector

```javascript

```

and letting all three consumers filter the parsed runs they need (title-token match, branch match, summary formatting). # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: third identical 4-status `listWorkflowRuns` fan-out — extract a shared helper**

`hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` re-implements the exact same per-status fan-out that already exists twice in this file:

- `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` (line ~334) — the gh-806 title-token latch
- `collectActiveWorkflowRuns` (line ~441) — the budget/summary collector

All three loop `['queued','in_progress','waiting','pending']`, call `scm.listWorkflowRuns(status, workflowFile, 50)`, wrap in the same try/`console.warn`/`continue`, and run through `parseWorkflowRuns`.
```javascript
// Returns { runsByStatus: { queued: [...], ... }, errors: [...] } — one fan-out.
function listActiveRunsByStatus(scm, workflowFile) { ... }
```

and letting all three consumers filter the parsed runs they need (title-token match, branch match, summary formatting).
